newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends down on bearish USDA data, soy drop.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends down on bearish USDA data, soy drop.

text.p: A bearish USDA crop report drove CBOT corn futures to a sharply lower close as did a limit plunge in the soy complex, traders said.

USDA early Friday said 1996 U.S. corn production would total 9.012 billion bushels, above an average trade estimate of 8.951 billion and up from the government's outlook in September for 8.804 billion bushels.
"There was not that much of an increase but everybody was scared by that nine in front of it," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
USDA also increased 1996-97 U.S. corn carryover to 903 million bushels from the previous 668 million bushel tally.
Traders said the collapse in soybean futures may have been as important to the decline in corn as were the USDA corn numbers.
"Everybody was surprised by the bean production," Kucha said. USDA increased its outlook for 1996 U.S. soybean production to 2.346 billion bushels from the previous forecast for 2.270 billion.
Corn closed 3-1/2 to seven cents per bushel lower, with December down 6-1/4 at $2.83-3/4.
Fund selling in corn totaled at least 15.0 million bushels with Refco Inc a key seller of eight million bushels of December and five million bushels of March, traders said.
December touched a session low of $2.83 per bushel, the lowest level for that month since December 6, 1995 when it last hit $2.83.
Technical indicators showed December's relative strength index (RSI) at the close at 20.947 points, near the generally perceived very oversold level of 20.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 65,000 contracts, up from 45,006 Thursday, according to the CBOT.

The corn options pit featured a Cargill Investor Service purchase of 1,000 March $2.90 puts at 11-1/2 to 12 cents, The Chicago Corp bought 400 December $2.70 puts at 2-1/2 cents and Prudential Securities sold 500 December $2.90 calls at five to 5-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 29,000 contracts, up from 25,922 Thursday.
